transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it’s really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I hope I'm not wasting your time, because I know it's probably nothing major, but... I guess what brings me in is that I've just been feeling so exhausted lately. 

And, well, it's in a way that sleep doesn't really seem to fix? Like, I'm still getting everything done—I'm a manager, so I always make sure to stay on top of my responsibilities—but just getting through a normal workday, and then trying to manage dinner at home... it all just feels so much heavier than it should right now. I don't know if that's the right way to explain it, or if that's a good enough reason to be here... does that make sense?
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Um... I really hate to use the word depressed, because I know so many people have it so much worse, and I really do have a lot to be thankful for. But... I suppose I have been feeling a little down. 

It's just... well, most days lately, I wake up with this sort of... heavy, gray feeling. It's almost like I'm already disappointed in the day before it even starts? I always try to shake it off right away, of course, and just get to work so it doesn't affect anyone else. I hope that doesn't sound like I'm just complaining... is it normal to feel like that sometimes?
Have you been enjoying things less than you usually do?

Um... well, maybe a little? I mean, I try to stay active, I really do, because I know how important it is to keep busy. But... normally, I absolutely love painting, and I usually spend my weekends just wandering through different museum exhibits. It's always been my favorite way to unwind. 

But recently... I don't know, I just leave my art supplies sitting there completely untouched. And when I think about going to a museum, I just... I can't seem to make myself care enough to actually go. I feel awful even admitting that, because I know I should be making the most of my free time instead of just letting it pass by. Does that sound like what you mean, or am I just being a bit lazy lately?
How have you been sleeping lately?

Um... well, I really try to keep a good schedule, you know? I make sure I'm in bed at a reasonable hour every night, because I know how important rest is for being productive the next day. But... I guess my sleep hasn't been the greatest lately. 

It's just that I'll wake up around four or five in the morning, and my mind just immediately starts going. I start thinking about work, and... well, things with my marriage, just normal stress, I'm sure. But once I'm awake like that, I'm just... done sleeping. I can't seem to drift off again, no matter how hard I try to relax. I know everyone has trouble sleeping sometimes when they have a lot on their plate, right? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm making a big deal out of nothing.
About how long have you been feeling this way?

Um... well, it's a little hard to pinpoint exactly, because I really try to just push through things, you know? But... I'd say this low feeling has been hanging around for about a month now. 

Before that, I was actually doing so well. I had this stretch where I was just incredibly energized, getting so much done at work, and I felt so driven. I was really proud of how productive I was being. But then... it just sort of shifted into this gray feeling I mentioned. I feel bad even bringing it up, because I know everyone has their ups and downs, right? Does a month seem like a long time to be stuck in a rut like this?
During that energized stretch before this low period, did you need less sleep than usual and still feel rested?

Um... well, yes, I suppose I did. But honestly, it felt really good at the time! I mean, I was just so focused and on top of everything. 

I think during that stretch, I was only sleeping maybe... four hours a night? Which I know sounds a little extreme, but I honestly didn't feel tired at all. I'd wake up and just feel completely ready to go. I'd be up early sending out work emails, sketching out new ideas for events we were planning, or even just... reorganizing the kitchen before anyone else was awake. It felt like I was finally getting ahead of my to-do list, you know? 

I hope that doesn't sound too strange. It's not necessarily a bad thing to be that productive on less sleep, is it? I just figured I was finally hitting my stride at work.
During that energized stretch, did you feel unusually happy or euphoric?

Um... I don't know if I'd use the word euphoric, exactly. That sounds a little extreme! But I did feel... really, really good. Earlier in the month, I just had this unusually charged, upbeat mood. I honestly felt brilliant, like every idea I had was just clicking perfectly. 

But... well, I do feel a little bad admitting this part... I guess I wasn't just happy the whole time. I'd have these moments where I was feeling great, but then I'd get irritated really fast if my husband questioned any of my plans. Which isn't really like me, I usually try to be very patient with him. I just felt so passionate about what I was doing, and it was frustrating to be slowed down, you know? It's normal to get a little defensive when you're that focused on your goals, isn't it? I hope I don't sound like a terrible wife for getting snappy with him.
During that energized stretch, did you do anything unusually risky or impulsive for you, like overspending?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I definitely wasn't doing anything crazy or risky, I promise! I'm usually very responsible with our finances and everything else. 

I guess... well, I might have bought a few extra things for the house that week, just because I was in such a good mood and wanted to spruce things up. But it wasn't anything we couldn't afford or anything completely out of the blue. I just felt really inspired, you know? It's okay to treat yourself a little bit when you're feeling that positive and productive, right? I certainly didn't do anything that would cause any real problems.
About how many days did that energized period last?

Um... let's see. I'd say it was probably... maybe around four or five days? 

I know that sounds like a long time to be running on so little sleep, but honestly, it just felt like a really good, productive week at work. It's not unusual to have a stretch where you're just really motivated and getting things done, right? I mean, everyone has weeks where they're just firing on all cylinders. I really hope it doesn't sound like I was out of control or anything, because I was actually getting a lot accomplished. It was just a few days of feeling really capable.
During that energized period, did it cause serious problems at work, at home, or in your relationships?

Um... no, definitely not serious problems! I mean, I was still going to work every day and taking care of things around the house. I always make sure to keep up with my responsibilities, I really do. 

I guess... well, if I'm being completely honest, maybe I wasn't quite at my best? Like, I've been a little slower making decisions at work lately, and... I might have flaked on a couple of family plans, which I feel terrible about. And I haven't been going to my art group as much, which usually keeps me pretty grounded. But I'm still functioning, you know? I'm still doing what I need to do. It's normal to just need a little step back sometimes to recharge, isn't it? I just don't want you to think I'm falling apart or letting anyone down.
During that energized stretch, were you talking a lot more than usual?

Um... well, maybe a little bit? I certainly didn't mean to be rude or dominate the conversation, I promise. I just had so many thoughts and ideas I wanted to get out. 

But, um... my husband did actually say something about it. And a couple of my coworkers, too. They told me I was talking so fast and jumping in so much that they couldn’t really get a word in. I felt terrible when they pointed it out! I was just so enthusiastic and eager to collaborate, and my brain was just moving a mile a minute. It’s normal to get a little carried away when you’re feeling that passionate about a project, isn't it? I really didn't mean to talk over anyone, and I've definitely made a point to be a much better listener since they mentioned it.
During that energized stretch, were you more active than usual or taking on more projects than you normally would?

Um... well, I suppose I was keeping pretty busy. I always try to be a team player at work, you know? So... I might have signed myself up to lead some extra pieces of our office morale program. And outside of work, I volunteered to help out with a few more Latino arts events than I usually do. 

I know it sounds like a lot, but I just felt so capable and I really wanted to help out. I mean, it's a good thing to be involved in your community and take initiative at your job, right? I didn't want anyone to think I was slacking off. I might have taken on a bit more than I normally would, but I just wanted to make sure everything was running smoothly. That's okay, isn't it? I just like being helpful.
During that energized stretch, did you feel unusually confident or like you had special abilities beyond your usual self?

Um... I wouldn't say I thought I had, like, superpowers or anything crazy like that! I just... I felt really capable. Like I finally had a clear vision of how to make things better for everyone.

I guess... well, I was honestly convinced that I could fix the whole department morale problem at work, and even completely overhaul our family routines at home. I just felt like I had the perfect plan, you know? And I really thought that if everyone would just get on board and follow my lead, everything would be so much smoother and happier. It's good to be confident in your ideas, right? I just wanted to help everyone get organized and feel better. I hope that doesn't make me sound arrogant or bossy... I really just wanted to be useful.
Lately, have you been having trouble concentrating or making decisions more than usual?

Um... well, maybe a little bit? I mean, I'm usually very on top of things, I promise. But lately... I guess my focus hasn't been quite as sharp as I'd like it to be. 

It's silly, really, but at work... I'll sit there with just a simple staffing email open, and I'll just reread it over and over. I just can't seem to decide what to say or which option makes the most sense. I know I should just make a choice and send it, but I get so worried about making the wrong call and messing things up for my team. It's normal to want to be careful and make the right decision, isn't it? I just don't want to let anyone down, so I end up second-guessing myself a lot. I hope my boss doesn't think I'm losing my touch... I'm really trying my best to stay focused.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of harming yourself?

Oh! Um... no, definitely not. I mean, I know I've been struggling a little bit lately, but I would never, ever want to do anything to hurt myself. 

I have my family, and my team at work really relies on me... I would never want to cause them any pain or be a burden like that. It's normal to just feel a little overwhelmed sometimes without actually wanting to give up, right? I promise I'm completely safe. I really hope you don't think I'm... you know, that things are that bad. I just want to get back to being my helpful self.
Lately, have you noticed your appetite being different than usual?

Um... well, maybe a little? I mean, I'm definitely still eating, I promise! It's just... I guess I haven't been super hungry lately. 

I've just been kind of picking at my meals, or... sometimes I get so caught up at work that I just completely forget to eat lunch. It's not a big deal, really, just being busy, you know? But I did notice that a few of my work skirts are fitting a little looser than usual, and I haven't been trying to lose weight or anything. I hope that's okay... it's pretty normal to lose your appetite a bit when you're feeling stressed or overwhelmed, right? I'm sure it's nothing to worry about, I just need to be better about making time for lunch.
